newsitem.title: INDIA: India says ports adequate to handle wheat imports.
newsitem.headline: India says ports adequate to handle wheat imports.

text.p: The Indian government said on Thursday it had made all arrangements at ports to handle two million tonnes of imported wheat, with the first shipment from Australia expected to reach India within 15 days.

"The first vessel 'Raja Mahendra' laden with 46,000 tonnes of wheat has already sailed from Australia on January 7 and is expected to arrive in India in around 15 days," the government said in a statement.
A few more ships from Australia were expected to reach India in January, the statement said.
It said about 180,000 tonnes of imported wheat was expected to arrive in January.
India last month decided to import two million tonnes of wheat in the current 1996/97 (April-March) fiscal year to augment domestic supplies and check rising prices.

India last imported wheat in 1992/93, buying two million tonnes of wheat. It exported 600,000 tonnes in 1995/96 and 1.07 million tonnes between April and September of this year, when the government halted exports.
The statment denied newpaper reports that port facilities were not adequate for handling wheat imports, saying the import of wheat was going "strictly as per schedule".
On Wednesday, state-run State Trading Corporation (STC) said it had contracted to import 1.25 million tonnes of wheat in 1996/97.
STC officials said India was focusing on Argentina, Australia and Canada as suppliers.

The statement said a task force had been created with officials from Food Ministry, Surface Transport Ministry, STC and the Food Corporation of India to facilitate the smooth handling of the imported wheat.
